runs.text: First, the leverage and coverage position is moderate and has improved. Gross debt over Adjusted EBITDA was 2.93x in FY2024 and 2.78x for the last twelve months to June 30, 2026, because between FY2024 and the last twelve months to June 30, 2026 Adjusted EBITDA rose 19.5% while debt principal rose 13.0%. Cash interest cover was 5.08x in FY2025 and 5.36x for the last twelve months [CP-1 leverage and interest cover tables]. The measure is the issuer's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back collections applied to principal, so it is a cash-collections measure and is not the covenant definition; ratios should not be compared with the 3.50x and 2.50x limits.

Second, reported profit is more estimate-driven than cash. In Q2 2026 changes in expected recoveries were USD 96.9 million of USD 153.3 million income from operations, after a European forecast review raised European ERC by USD 348.5 million and added approximately USD 105 million to changes in expected future recoveries [CP-1; CP-1A revenue model row; Q2 10-Q page:9]. The USD 348.5 million is an ERC change and not income. Cash collections of USD 558.5 million in the quarter are the firmer measure.

Third, liquidity depends on the borrowing base. Cash is USD 132.4 million against availability of USD 998.5 million, of which USD 733.1 million, 73.4%, is based on current ERC at advance rates of 35% for Core and 55% for Insolvency pools [CP-1 liquidity tables; 10-K page:87]. A downward ERC revision would cut capacity at the moment it is most needed. Cash and availability total USD 1,130.9 million, 4.57x the USD 247.7 million of interest, unused fees and principal payments the company estimates for the next 12 months (Q2 10-Q page:42).

Fourth, purchasing, not operations, drives the debt trend. Adjusted EBITDA after cash interest, cash taxes and capital expenditure was short of cash spent on portfolio purchases by USD 190.7 million in FY2025 and USD 502.9 million in FY2024 [CP-1 bridge]. Borrowings rose in both years. Management says it can slow purchases without hurting current-year collections (10-K page:55), which is a management claim, but forward flow agreements carry few minimum obligations [CP-1A operating model], so the lever exists in the documents.

Fifth, refinancing risk is deferred and then concentrated. The European revolving facility now matures on April 30, 2031, the 2028 senior notes of USD 398.0 million fall due on February 1, 2028 (about 15 months after the as-of date), and USD 1,837.1 million, 48.7% of principal, matures in 2029 across both other revolvers, the 2029 notes and the term loan [CP-1 maturity table].

Sixth, structure and visibility are unresolved. Credit facilities of USD 2,130.6 million, 56.5% of principal, are secured by liens on U.S. and UK assets and on European subsidiary equity, and the USD 1,640.6 million of senior notes are unsecured [CP-1 debt table; 10-K page:87 to page:92]. About 60% of debt is fixed or hedged, and a 50 basis point move changes annual interest by an estimated USD 7.8 million (Q2 10-Q page:46). The notes' guarantor structure, the credit agreement definitions and the covenant ratios are not supplied.

runs.text: Strengths. The company has a long-dated, diversified liability stack: secured revolving facilities in several currencies, a term loan and unsecured notes, with no principal beyond term loan payments due for about 15 months and revolvers running to 2029 and 2031. Cash earning power is growing: cash collections of USD 558.5 million in Q2 2026 are 4.2% above Q2 2025, ERC is USD 8,894.5 million, 2.36x debt principal, and Adjusted EBITDA has risen 9.6% year on year. Purchasing is discretionary, which gives management a lever over debt growth. The European business is organised so that portfolio ownership and collections sit in the same entity, and the European and UK facilities are multi-currency to match funding by currency (10-K page:65). The company is widely held, with no sponsor, no dividends in three years and a documented early extension of its European facility, and it discloses reconciliations of its non-GAAP measures and ERC revisions.

Weaknesses. Earnings, ERC and the ERC-based part of availability depend on internal models and forecasts, and a USD 412.6 million goodwill impairment in Q3 2025 shows that valuations can reset sharply. Cash on hand is small, USD 132.4 million against USD 3,771.3 million of debt, so liquidity is a function of revolver access and covenant compliance, which cannot be observed. Debt has grown faster than cash after purchases in two consecutive years, and shareholder returns continue through repurchases, with a USD 150 million program approved on August 3, 2026. Europe is 54.0% of ERC, adding currency and fragmented regulatory exposure, and the U.S. segment's adjusted operating income was flat year on year in Q2 2026 as legal collection spending rose. A multi-state Attorneys General investigation open since 2015 remains unresolved. The 2029 maturity cluster and the structural position of unsecured noteholders behind secured facilities add refinancing and ranking sensitivity.

runs.text: No acquisition, take-private, merger or other ownership transaction is described in the supplied sources, and the context holds no deal terms, so the transaction view is Insufficient Information for any pending or announced ownership event as of 2026-11-05; the sources end on August 7, 2026. The financing and portfolio transactions that are described are as follows. On September 30, 2025 the company completed a private offering of EUR 300.0 million (US$352.4 million at issuance) of 6.250% senior notes due September 30, 2032 through its wholly owned subsidiary PRA Group Europe Holding II S.à r.l.; the notes are senior unsecured obligations of that issuer, guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by PRA Group, Inc. and by the domestic restricted subsidiaries that guarantee the North American facility, with interest payable on March 31 and September 30, a change of control put at 101%, and a call schedule at 103.125% from September 30, 2028 falling to par from 2030 (10-K page:90). The use of proceeds is not stated in the pages read, so it is Insufficient Information; the cash flow statement shows the proceeds within financing activities (10-K page:71) and the company describes the issue as its first euro-denominated senior notes (10-K page:38). On April 30, 2026 the company amended and restated its European revolving credit facility: the maturity moved from November 23, 2027 to April 30, 2031, the maximum ERC ratio fell from 45.0% to 40.0%, and, subject to conditions, borrowers may make investments in or loans to joint ventures up to EUR 100 million; the Q1 2026 10-Q reports the aggregate revolving borrowings available and funding costs as unchanged (Q1 10-Q page:17; Q2 10-Q page:11). The joint venture basket is a new permission that could move value outside the borrower group, but its use is not evidenced and the agreement is not supplied. Earlier debt history inside the sources: in 2024 the company issued 8.875% senior notes due January 31, 2030 ($400.0 million on May 20, 2024 and a further $150.0 million on November 25, 2024 at 103.625% of principal) and retired 2025 senior notes (10-K page:91; Q3 10-Q page:6; 10-K page:71). Other events: the April 2025 sale of the 11.7% interest in RCB Investimentos S.A. with a gain of $38.4 million, stated not to affect ownership of the portfolio investments in South America (10-K page:43); the Q3 2025 goodwill impairment, recognised after a quantitative test that compared fair value with market capitalization (Q3 10-Q page:12); and, as a subsequent event to the June 30, 2026 balance sheet, the August 3, 2026 board approval of a new share repurchase program of up to $150 million, subject to covenants and board discretion (Q2 10-Q page:21). The new program follows repurchases of $20.0 million in 2025 and $20.0 million in the first half of 2026 (10-K page:38; Q2 10-Q page:15). Amounts of each financing and the debt table are in the CP-1 handoff.

fields.value: - Maturity schedule: the 10-K principal payments table (page:86) is stated as of December 31, 2025 and carries the European facility at its earlier maturity. The Q2 10-Q (page:11, page:42) states the extension from November 23, 2027 to April 30, 2031 and that principal payments on borrowings run from February 2028 through September 2032, apart from quarterly term loan payments. For June 30, 2026 maturity work, the Q2 10-Q controls and the 10-K table must not be reused unadjusted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant terms: the 10-K prints covenant tests per facility (page:87 to page:89), including a maximum ERC ratio of 45% on the European facility. The Q2 10-Q (page:11) states that the amendment reduced it to 40%. The Q2 10-Q confirms compliance as of June 30, 2026 (page:11, page:42) but prints no actual ratio level, and refers to the 10-K for facility detail. The Q1 10-Q (page:17) lists the changes "among other modifications" and says the aggregate revolving borrowings available and funding costs remained unchanged. Whether other European covenant terms changed on amendment is not verifiable without the amended agreement, which the Q2 10-Q lists as Exhibit 10.1 filed with that report (page:48) and which is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Availability: availability is printed by facility at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:54), March 31, 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:32) and June 30, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:40 and page:41). It is split into an amount based on current ERC and an additional amount subject to borrowing base and advance rates. Availability is therefore tied to ERC and to the borrowing base definitions, which are not supplied in full.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - ERC: the European ERC step-up is $348.5 million per the Q2 10-Q (page:24) and approximately $349 million per the Q2 release (page:1), a rounding difference. The Q2 10-Q (page:9) states the positive adjustment to changes in expected future recoveries from the European forecast update was approximately $105 million, with partial offsets in other pools; the total positive adjustment to changes in expected future recoveries for the quarter is $74.2 million (page:9). Headline ERC change and income effect are different measures, and a consumer must carry both.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Non-GAAP: Adjusted EBITDA is printed by the issuer for the last twelve months ended June 30, 2026 and for fiscal 2025 (Q2 release page:11), and its definition adds back recoveries collected and applied to finance receivables less changes in expected recoveries. It is a management non-GAAP measure, labelled as such in the 10-Q (page:24, page:35). The Q2 10-Q key metrics table (page:25) prints the last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA for both periods behind the stated 9.6% increase; the Q2 release reconciliation (page:11) prints the June 30, 2026 last-twelve-months and fiscal 2025 columns only, so the prior-year reconciliation is not supplied.

fields.value: The reported base is complete for the audited year ended December 31, 2025, the comparative year 2024 and the interim periods to June 30, 2026. On the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA, gross debt (credit facilities plus senior notes, at principal) was $3,771.3 million at June 30, 2026 against last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of $1,358.9 million, which is 2.78x gross and 2.68x after deducting cash and cash equivalents of $132.4 million. Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid 5.36x. Total availability under the credit facilities was $998.5 million, of which $733.1 million is based on current ERC and $265.4 million is subject to borrowing base and advance rates. Quarterly cash collections were $558.5 million in Q2 2026. Three features limit how far these numbers can be pushed. First, PRA's Adjusted EBITDA adds back recoveries collected and applied to finance receivables less changes in expected recoveries, so it is a cash-collections measure and is not comparable with a conventional EBITDA; it is also not the EBITDA defined in the credit agreements, which is not supplied. Second, net cash used in operating activities is negative in every year shown because collections applied to principal are classified in investing activities, so operating cash flow and a free cash flow built from it are not meaningful here. Third, Q2 2026 earnings include a European forecast revision: changes in expected recoveries were $96.9 million of income from operations of $153.3 million. The base does not support a covenant headroom conclusion: compliance is stated but no covenant ratio is printed.

fields.value: PRA Group, Inc. is a Delaware specialty finance company headquartered in Norfolk, Virginia that buys nonperforming consumer loans from banks, consumer finance companies, auto finance providers and other creditors, and collects on them over several years through call centers, external vendors, legal recovery and digital channels (10-K page:6 to page:8). It reports two segments, the U.S. and Europe, created in Q4 2025 after a new chief executive officer was appointed in 2025 (10-K page:103), plus smaller operations in South America, Canada and Australia. Revenue is accrued from the expected collections of each portfolio, so reported profit depends on management's collection forecasts; the filing itself calls Portfolio income the more predictable component and Changes in expected recoveries the estimate-driven one (Q2 10-Q page:29). The company is publicly listed with 44 holders of record and no sponsor, parent or controlling holder is disclosed in the supplied sources; the proxy statement that would give beneficial ownership is not supplied. No acquisition, take-private or other ownership transaction is described in the supplied sources. The transactions that are described are financing and portfolio events: the September 30, 2025 issue of euro-denominated 6.250% senior notes due 2032 by a Luxembourg subsidiary, the April 30, 2026 amendment and extension of the European revolving credit facility, the April 2025 sale of an 11.7% interest in a Brazilian servicing company, and the August 3, 2026 approval of a new share repurchase program. Creditor-relevant change is concentrated in three areas: the June 30, 2026 European forecast review that raised European ERC by $348.5 million; the cost and organisation programme under the "PRA 3.0" strategy (management's term); and capital returns through repurchases while portfolio purchases are financed with debt. Documented actions show no priming, uptiering, drop-down or related-party leakage, but the legal capacity under the credit agreements and indentures cannot be assessed because those documents are not supplied.

The financing and portfolio transactions that are described are as follows. On September 30, 2025 the company completed a private offering of EUR 300.0 million (US$352.4 million at issuance) of 6.250% senior notes due September 30, 2032 through its wholly owned subsidiary PRA Group Europe Holding II S.à r.l.; the notes are senior unsecured obligations of that issuer, guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by PRA Group, Inc. and by the domestic restricted subsidiaries that guarantee the North American facility, with interest payable on March 31 and September 30, a change of control put at 101%, and a call schedule at 103.125% from September 30, 2028 falling to par from 2030 (10-K page:90). The use of proceeds is not stated in the pages read, so it is Insufficient Information; the cash flow statement shows the proceeds within financing activities (10-K page:71) and the company describes the issue as its first euro-denominated senior notes (10-K page:38). On April 30, 2026 the company amended and restated its European revolving credit facility: the maturity moved from November 23, 2027 to April 30, 2031, the maximum ERC ratio fell from 45.0% to 40.0%, and, subject to conditions, borrowers may make investments in or loans to joint ventures up to EUR 100 million; the Q1 2026 10-Q reports the aggregate revolving borrowings available and funding costs as unchanged (Q1 10-Q page:17; Q2 10-Q page:11). The joint venture basket is a new permission that could move value outside the borrower group, but its use is not evidenced and the agreement is not supplied. Earlier debt history inside the sources: in 2024 the company issued 8.875% senior notes due January 31, 2030 ($400.0 million on May 20, 2024 and a further $150.0 million on November 25, 2024 at 103.625% of principal) and retired 2025 senior notes (10-K page:91; Q3 10-Q page:6; 10-K page:71). Other events: the April 2025 sale of the 11.7% interest in RCB Investimentos S.A. with a gain of $38.4 million, stated not to affect ownership of the portfolio investments in South America (10-K page:43); the Q3 2025 goodwill impairment, recognised after a quantitative test that compared fair value with market capitalization (Q3 10-Q page:12); and, as a subsequent event to the June 30, 2026 balance sheet, the August 3, 2026 board approval of a new share repurchase program of up to $150 million, subject to covenants and board discretion (Q2 10-Q page:21). The new program follows repurchases of $20.0 million in 2025 and $20.0 million in the first half of 2026 (10-K page:38; Q2 10-Q page:15). Amounts of each financing and the debt table are in the CP-1 handoff.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PRA Group's fundamental credit is adequate and stable, with moderate leverage that depends on forecast accuracy more than on a cash buffer. The strongest support is cash earning power: last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,358.9 million covers cash interest of USD 253.4 million 5.36x, gross debt is 2.78x that EBITDA, and no principal other than term loan payments is due before February 2028. The weakest point is that revenue, ERC and ERC-linked availability of USD 998.5 million all rest on internal collection forecasts, while purchases have exceeded post-interest cash earnings in each of the last two years. What decides the outcome is whether collections keep matching forecasts and whether purchasing is held to the cash the business generates. Covenant headroom cannot be observed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, the leverage and coverage position is moderate and has improved. Gross debt over Adjusted EBITDA was 2.93x in FY2024 and 2.78x for the last twelve months to June 30, 2026, because between FY2024 and the last twelve months to June 30, 2026 Adjusted EBITDA rose 19.5% while debt principal rose 13.0%. Cash interest cover was 5.08x in FY2025 and 5.36x for the last twelve months [CP-1 leverage and interest cover tables]. The measure is the issuer's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back collections applied to principal, so it is a cash-collections measure and is not the covenant definition; ratios should not be compared with the 3.50x and 2.50x limits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, reported profit is more estimate-driven than cash. In Q2 2026 changes in expected recoveries were USD 96.9 million of USD 153.3 million income from operations, after a European forecast review raised European ERC by USD 348.5 million and added approximately USD 105 million to changes in expected future recoveries [CP-1; CP-1A revenue model row; Q2 10-Q page:9]. The USD 348.5 million is an ERC change and not income. Cash collections of USD 558.5 million in the quarter are the firmer measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, liquidity depends on the borrowing base. Cash is USD 132.4 million against availability of USD 998.5 million, of which USD 733.1 million, 73.4%, is based on current ERC at advance rates of 35% for Core and 55% for Insolvency pools [CP-1 liquidity tables; 10-K page:87]. A downward ERC revision would cut capacity at the moment it is most needed. Cash and availability total USD 1,130.9 million, 4.57x the USD 247.7 million of interest, unused fees and principal payments the company estimates for the next 12 months (Q2 10-Q page:42).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, purchasing, not operations, drives the debt trend. Adjusted EBITDA after cash interest, cash taxes and capital expenditure was short of cash spent on portfolio purchases by USD 190.7 million in FY2025 and USD 502.9 million in FY2024 [CP-1 bridge]. Borrowings rose in both years. Management says it can slow purchases without hurting current-year collections (10-K page:55), which is a management claim, but forward flow agreements carry few minimum obligations [CP-1A operating model], so the lever exists in the documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, refinancing risk is deferred and then concentrated. The European revolving facility now matures on April 30, 2031, the 2028 senior notes of USD 398.0 million fall due on February 1, 2028 (about 15 months after the as-of date), and USD 1,837.1 million, 48.7% of principal, matures in 2029 across both other revolvers, the 2029 notes and the term loan [CP-1 maturity table].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, structure and visibility are unresolved. Credit facilities of USD 2,130.6 million, 56.5% of principal, are secured by liens on U.S. and UK assets and on European subsidiary equity, and the USD 1,640.6 million of senior notes are unsecured [CP-1 debt table; 10-K page:87 to page:92]. About 60% of debt is fixed or hedged, and a 50 basis point move changes annual interest by an estimated USD 7.8 million (Q2 10-Q page:46). The notes' guarantor structure, the credit agreement definitions and the covenant ratios are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. The company has a long-dated, diversified liability stack: secured revolving facilities in several currencies, a term loan and unsecured notes, with no principal beyond term loan payments due for about 15 months and revolvers running to 2029 and 2031. Cash earning power is growing: cash collections of USD 558.5 million in Q2 2026 are 4.2% above Q2 2025, ERC is USD 8,894.5 million, 2.36x debt principal, and Adjusted EBITDA has risen 9.6% year on year. Purchasing is discretionary, which gives management a lever over debt growth. The European business is organised so that portfolio ownership and collections sit in the same entity, and the European and UK facilities are multi-currency to match funding by currency (10-K page:65). The company is widely held, with no sponsor, no dividends in three years and a documented early extension of its European facility, and it discloses reconciliations of its non-GAAP measures and ERC revisions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Earnings, ERC and the ERC-based part of availability depend on internal models and forecasts, and a USD 412.6 million goodwill impairment in Q3 2025 shows that valuations can reset sharply. Cash on hand is small, USD 132.4 million against USD 3,771.3 million of debt, so liquidity is a function of revolver access and covenant compliance, which cannot be observed. Debt has grown faster than cash after purchases in two consecutive years, and shareholder returns continue through repurchases, with a USD 150 million program approved on August 3, 2026. Europe is 54.0% of ERC, adding currency and fragmented regulatory exposure, and the U.S. segment's adjusted operating income was flat year on year in Q2 2026 as legal collection spending rose. A multi-state Attorneys General investigation open since 2015 remains unresolved. The 2029 maturity cluster and the structural position of unsecured noteholders behind secured facilities add refinancing and ranking sensitivity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PRA Group is an adequately financed, moderately levered collector of nonperforming loans whose debt service is supported by growing cash collections but whose reported earnings, ERC and ERC-linked liquidity rest on internal forecasts and whose debt keeps rising to fund portfolio purchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit work for PRA Group is traceable enough for committee use with restrictions, because every headline figure rests on filed statements and recomputes exactly. The strongest support is that leverage, cover, liquidity and maturity numbers all agree with printed inputs, and management claims are tagged as management language rather than fact. The weakest point is that no executed credit agreement or indenture is supplied, so covenant headroom, ranking and guarantor statements rest on filing summaries and cannot be traced to primary legal text. The outcome turns on whether those documents and any report for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 can be obtained; until then conclusions that depend on them stay restricted. One material framing defect and six minor defects are logged for correction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scope and method. Every numeric claim in the Reader summary rows and key tables of CP-1, CP-1A and CP-2 was opened at its cited page or located on a neighbouring page of the same source; every number in the CP-1 financial table was checked against the cited statements by search; and every derived figure (CP-1 C1 to C9, CP-2 K1 to K9) was recomputed from its printed inputs. Narrative sentences were traced where they carry a number, a date or a legal characterisation. Prose without figures (for example descriptive business text) was sampled and not exhaustively traced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Result. No unsupported headline claim, no figure without a source and no arithmetic error was found. Identity, as-of date and source hashes in the upstream handoffs match the run. Management characterisations ("record ERC levels", competitive strengths, ability to slow purchases) are tagged Management Language. Two analyst constructs (illustrative cash bridge, cost-adjusted ERC cover) are labelled as such. Confidence score and band are not computed here because the scoring script is not available in this host run; the Medium confidence stated is a judgment.
